questions.question:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘÷ ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘−’ are interchanged?

88 ÷ 18 × 28 + 4 − 14 =?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2381f95ecfcbe7f6eaceba831d02f99bf624c84151895e65ac4d5a630f47ff34.png] 

Given equation: 88 ÷ 18 × 28 + 4 − 14 = ?

After interchanging ‘+’ and ‘÷’ and ‘×’ and ‘−’, we get:

88 + 18 − 28 ÷ 4 × 14 = ?

Following the BODMAS:

= 88 + 18 − __**28 ÷ 4**__ × 14

= 88 + 18 − __**7 × 14**__

= __**88 + 18**__ − 98

= __**106 − 98**__

= 8

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All irons are heaters.

Some irons are fans.

Conclusions:

(i) Some heaters are fans.

(ii) All fans are irons.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c6c8ce5456d60918527df284831865e4fd236820da307a6d4c171738ccf020b.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b55396b3c6e6cbf4e89681698c851a7f34c7a75f0c4018a69f17083707cc47d9.png] 

**Conclusions:**

(i) Some heaters are fans → **True **(As, All irons are heaters, Some irons are fans. so, Some heaters are fans holds true).

(ii) All fans are irons → False (As, Some irons are fans. so, All fans are irons can be a possibility but not definite).

Thus, Only conclusion I follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
Six people A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting third to the right of C. D is sitting second to the right of A. A and E are immediate neighbours. E is sitting second to the right of B.

How many people are sitting between E and C when counted from the left of E?
questions.solution:
Given:

Six people A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre.

D is sitting second to the right of A.

A and E are immediate neighbours.

E is sitting second to the right of B.

F is sitting third to the right of C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10746b52f0532e110d89efa8bf5ef626a9a75e915cf59d800532af8635c54c84.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7fc1a2a737c918e946dc47dda9014484d39a452d697450d92329361062fad2d5.png] 

Thus, 3 people are sitting between E and C when counted from the left of E.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question:
In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

246, 123

448, 224
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: The second number is exactly half of the first number.**

**2nd number = 1st number ÷ 2**

**For (246, 123):**

→ 2nd number = 246 ÷ 2

→ 2nd number = 123

**For (448, 224):**

→ 2nd number = 448 ÷ 2

→ 2nd number = 224

**Option 1) (624, 312)**

→ 2nd number = 624 ÷ 2

→ 2nd number = 312

→ This option follows the logic.

**Option 2) (102, 226)**

→ 2nd number = 102 ÷ 2

→ 2nd number = 51

→ Since 51 ≠ 226, this option does not follow the logic.

**Option 3) (325, 96)**

→ 2nd number = 325 ÷ 2

→ 2nd number = 162.5

→ Since 162.5 ≠ 96, this option does not follow the logic

**Option 4) (444, 66)**

→ 2nd number = 444 ÷ 2

→ 2nd number = 222

→ Since 222 ≠ 66, this option does not follow the logic.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.
